title: Treatment of brain inflammatory diseases by delivering exosome encapsulated anti-inflammatory drugs from the nasal region to the brain
excerpt: Curated summary: in mouse models, intranasal exosomes carrying curcumin or a STAT3 inhibitor were reported to reach brain microglia and improve model-specific inflammatory or tumor outcomes. These findings are preclinical and formulation-specific.

title: Intranasal MSC-derived A1-exosomes ease inflammation, and prevent abnormal neurogenesis and memory dysfunction after status epilepticus
excerpt: Curated summary: after status epilepticus in young mice, intranasally administered human MSC-derived EVs were reported in the hippocampus and were associated with reduced neuronal loss and inflammation and preservation of neurogenesis and cognitive or memory outcomes versus vehicle.

title: Extracellular vesicles from immortalized mesenchymal stromal cells protect against neonatal hypoxic-ischemic brain injury
excerpt: Curated summary: repeated intranasal EV administration after hypoxic-ischemic injury reduced brain tissue atrophy in neonatal mice; EVs from a clonal immortalized MSC line and primary MSCs showed comparable effects. The study frames source-cell consistency and scale as translational considerations.

title: Minimal information for studies of extracellular vesicles (MISEV2023): From basic to advanced approaches
excerpt: Curated summary: the ISEV consensus identifies continuing challenges in EV nomenclature, separation from non-vesicular particles, characterization, functional studies, production reporting, and in-vivo evaluation; it recommends transparent, orthogonal characterization and appropriate controls.

title: Pharmacokinetics and biodistribution of extracellular vesicles administered intravenously and intranasally to Macaca nemestrina
excerpt: Curated summary: reporter-labeled Expi293F-derived EVs administered intranasally to macaques were not reliably detected above background in CSF, showed negligible brain uptake, and were strongly retained in nasal lavage. EV source, formulation, labeling, administration, and species may affect generalizability.
